title: 北京上空的绿火球，是啥？
title_en: What Was the Green Fireball over Beijing?

segments.zh: 昨晚六点半，北京上空
segments.en: Last night at 6:30, over Beijing,

segments.zh: 一个大火球拖着绿光往下砸。
segments.en: a huge fireball fell trailing green light.

segments.zh: 河北、山西的网友也拍到了，
segments.en: People in Hebei and Shanxi filmed it too;

segments.zh: 天文馆专家说：多半是同一颗。
segments.en: planetarium experts say it was probably the same one.

segments.zh: 一颗流星，
segments.en: One meteor,

segments.zh: 照亮了三个省。
segments.en: lighting up three provinces.

segments.zh: 今天的烧脑问题：一块太空石头，
segments.en: Today's brain teaser: how can a space rock

segments.zh: 凭什么亮成这样，还带绿光？
segments.en: glow this bright, and green?

segments.zh: 认识主角：小火，
segments.en: Meet our hero, Blaze,

segments.zh: 一块在太空飘了很久的石头。
segments.en: a rock that drifted in space for ages.

segments.zh: 它绕着太阳跑，
segments.en: It circled the Sun,

segments.zh: 正好撞上了地球。
segments.en: and ran right into Earth.

segments.zh: 撞进来有多快？
segments.en: How fast?

segments.zh: 流星一般每秒十几到七十多公里。
segments.en: Meteors hit at roughly 11 to 72 km per second.

segments.zh: 每秒几十公里，
segments.en: Tens of km per second:

segments.zh: 比步枪子弹快几十倍。
segments.en: dozens of times faster than a rifle bullet.

segments.zh: 反转一：它发光，
segments.en: Twist one:

segments.zh: 主要不是因为摩擦。
segments.en: it does not glow mainly from friction.

segments.zh: 它太快了，前面的空气来不及让开，
segments.en: It is so fast the air ahead cannot get out of the way,

segments.zh: 被挤得越来越紧。
segments.en: and gets squeezed tighter and tighter.

segments.zh: 就像打气筒，
segments.en: Like a bike pump:

segments.zh: 压得越狠，筒越烫。
segments.en: the harder you squeeze, the hotter it gets.

segments.zh: 被压缩的空气烫到几千度，
segments.en: The squeezed air reaches thousands of degrees,

segments.zh: 把石头表面烤化、烤成气。
segments.en: melting and vaporizing the rock's skin.

segments.zh: 这团热气和空气一起发光，
segments.en: That hot gas glows along with the air.

segments.zh: 这就是流星。
segments.en: That is a meteor.

segments.zh: 反转二：为啥是绿的？
segments.en: Twist two: why green?

segments.zh: 颜色是原子的“指纹”。
segments.en: Color is an atom's fingerprint.

segments.zh: 每种原子被烤“兴奋”了，
segments.en: Each kind of atom, when heated up,

segments.zh: 只放出自己那几种颜色的光。
segments.en: gives off only its own few colors.

segments.zh: 就像烟花：钠是黄的，
segments.en: Like fireworks: sodium is yellow,

segments.zh: 锶是红的。
segments.en: strontium is red.

segments.zh: 流星里的镁、镍，还有空气里的氧，
segments.en: Magnesium and nickel in the rock, plus oxygen in the air,

segments.zh: 常被认为是绿光的来源。
segments.en: are the usual suspects for green.

segments.zh: 黄色常来自钠，
segments.en: Yellow often comes from sodium,

segments.zh: 红色常来自空气里的氮和氧。
segments.en: red from nitrogen and oxygen in the air.

segments.zh: 所以网友看到的绿、黄、红，
segments.en: So the green, yellow and red people saw

segments.zh: 其实是一张化学成分表。
segments.en: is really a chemistry report.

segments.zh: 反转三：为啥北京、河北、山西
segments.en: Twist three: how could Beijing, Hebei and Shanxi

segments.zh: 都能看到同一颗？
segments.en: all see the same one?

segments.zh: 因为流星多半在七八十公里以上发光，
segments.en: Meteors usually glow 70 km up or higher,

segments.zh: 比飞机高差不多十倍。
segments.en: about ten times higher than airliners.

segments.zh: 站得越高，看得越远；
segments.en: The higher you stand, the farther you see;

segments.zh: 反过来，越高的东西，越多地方能看到它。
segments.en: and the higher a thing is, the more places can see it.

segments.zh: 新华社报道，山西阳泉的监测点也拍到了，
segments.en: Xinhua says monitors in Yangquan, Shanxi caught it too,

segments.zh: 我们估算离北京三百来公里。
segments.en: about 300 km from Beijing by our estimate.

segments.zh: 天文学上，比金星还亮的流星，
segments.en: In astronomy, a meteor brighter than Venus

segments.zh: 就叫火流星。
segments.en: is called a fireball.

segments.zh: 专家估计这颗“比较大个儿”，
segments.en: Experts think this one was fairly big,

segments.zh: 可能留下了陨石。
segments.en: and may have dropped meteorites.

segments.zh: 大部分石头在半空就烧光了，
segments.en: Most of the rock burns up high in the sky.

segments.zh: 撑到地面的那一点才叫陨石。
segments.en: The bits that reach the ground are meteorites.

segments.zh: 最后那一段它不亮了：
segments.en: The last stretch is dark:

segments.zh: 空气把它刹得很慢，像普通石头一样掉。
segments.en: the air brakes it until it just drops like a stone.

segments.zh: 地球每天要挨多少太空石头？
segments.en: How much space stuff hits Earth each day?

segments.zh: 常见估计：几十吨。
segments.en: A common estimate: tens of tons.

segments.zh: 绝大多数比沙粒还小，
segments.en: Almost all of it is smaller than sand grains,

segments.zh: 你根本看不见。
segments.en: far too small to see.

segments.zh: 友情提示：目前还没有找到陨石的报道，
segments.en: Fine print: no meteorite has been reported found yet.

segments.zh: “可能”只是可能。
segments.en: Maybe means maybe.

segments.zh: 真捡到可疑的石头，
segments.en: If you find a suspicious rock,

segments.zh: 先拍照、记位置，再联系天文馆。
segments.en: photograph it, note the spot, and call a planetarium.

segments.zh: 想看流星？
segments.en: Want to see one?

segments.zh: 找个远离灯光的地方，抬头多等一会儿。
segments.en: Find a dark spot, look up, and be patient.

segments.zh: 所以小火凭什么亮成这样？
segments.en: So why did Blaze glow so bright?

segments.zh: 速度太快，把空气压烫了。
segments.en: It was so fast it crushed the air red hot.

segments.zh: 为啥带绿光？
segments.en: Why green?

segments.zh: 原子在报自己的名字。
segments.en: The atoms were calling out their names.

segments.zh: 一块石头在太空飘了几十亿年，
segments.en: A rock that drifted for billions of years

segments.zh: 最后五秒，给三个省放了场烟花。
segments.en: spent its last five seconds as fireworks for three provinces.
